question: Does the existing complete PNG/JPEG integrity decode have a demonstrated, bounded memory cost for browser-produced screenshots, and can a safe pixel cap be selected from current policy?

source_review.capture_path: Active explicit screenshot handler (playwright-driver/src/handlers/screenshot.ts) defaults fullPage=true when omitted. Passive telemetry (playwright-driver/src/telemetry/screenshot.ts) is viewport-only by default; fullPage is opt-in via SCREENSHOT_FULL_PAGE=true. Either path can produce full-page output when explicitly requested or configured.
source_review.input_constraints: Driver request parsing rejects request bodies over 5 MiB, and the API writer defaults to a 4 MiB encoded screenshot retention limit. No decoded-pixel or decoder-memory budget is declared.
source_review.decoder_behavior: Go 1.26 standard-library PNG decoding allocates image.NewNRGBA/NewRGBA/NewNRGBA64 buffers from header dimensions; JPEG decoding allocates raster buffers from image bounds. DecodeConfig alone does not prove complete image integrity, as retained truncated-PNG regression demonstrates.
source_review.threat_boundary: The driver is local, but arbitrary website content can influence dimensions of an explicit full-page screenshot or opted-in full-page telemetry. A bounded hostile-dimension decode was not executed because the active process memory envelope is not established.

writer_benchmark.fixture: 1280x720 fixed-pattern PNG through full writer and in-memory screenshot storage
writer_benchmark.interpretation: One local isolated workload only; does not bound hostile dimensions or establish end-to-end browser latency.

inventory.scope_note: Shared worktree contains other BAS modifications; preserve them and interpret this digest only as this scan's selected source population.

decision.documentation_change: Corrected ArtifactLimitsConfig.MaxScreenshotBytes comment: encoded images are omitted intact when over limit, not truncated.
decision.pixel_cap: Not selected. The repository declares no decoder-memory budget; a cap would be unsupported policy. A safe streaming PNG/JPEG integrity validator or explicit runtime budget may provide a grounded next step.
decision.issue_disposition: RF060 remains resolved for integrity and receipt validation; decoded-memory bound and end-to-end capture cost remain unqualified.

next_action: Establish a resource budget for the managed local driver/API path and validate realistic full-page dimensions in a controlled browser fixture. Do not execute a hostile-size full decode before a safe memory envelope exists.
